title: TickTick Automation Setup and Plan Limits in 2026
summary: TickTick automation starts with recurring tasks, reminders, and email-to-task, then adds external connectors as needed. Determine which approach suits you.
body_markdown:
## Fix TickTick automation errors and limits


Check your largest list against the table before blaming the connector. Most automation failures come from hitting a plan cap or a broken connector login, and the caps are the easier half because TickTick publishes them.


### Plan and quota limits


Limit Free Premium Source page


Lists 9 299[TickTick upgrade](https://ticktick.com/upgrade)


Tasks per list 99 999[TickTick upgrade](https://ticktick.com/upgrade)


Subtasks per task 19 199[TickTick upgrade](https://ticktick.com/upgrade)


Reminders per task 2 5[TickTick upgrade](https://ticktick.com/upgrade)


> Most automation failures come from hitting a plan cap or a broken connector login, and the caps are the easier half because TickTick publishes them.


Create a list per client or per project and the automation stops working at the tenth, because the free cap is 9 lists.


Push every email or form entry into one inbox list and it will start failing once that list holds 99 tasks, the free cap per list.


At the twentieth subtask a checklist generator will break, because free accounts also stop at 19 subtasks per task.


The 2-reminder limit matters most if a connector adds a reminder at creation, because it leaves one slot for you.


### TickTick authorisation and sync errors


When a connector run fails with an authorisation error, reconnect the TickTick account inside the connector before changing anything else. A token that has expired or been revoked looks the same as a bad trigger, so reconnecting rules it out in under a minute.


If the run succeeds but the task never appears on your phone, the write went through and the app hasn't synced. Pull to refresh before you rebuild the workflow.


If a bulk import fails partway, split it into smaller batches and add a delay between runs. The TickTick pages I was given publish no API rate limit, so that's a workaround, not a documented threshold.


### TickTick time zone and repeat task problems


When a connector sends UTC and your account is set to a local zone, tasks created with a due time can land hours off. Test with one task due "today at 17:00" and compare it with what the app shows.


If they differ, set the zone explicitly in the connector's field mapping.


Watch repeats as well, the other weak spot. A connector that creates a task with a repeat rule may not re-create it correctly when you complete it.


The sources I have don't describe how completion interacts with repeats, so test one repeating task through a full cycle before you rely on it.
